Decision record and eight testable requirements

The diagram identifies every source and consumer, without private client details.

All ten invalid cases fail explicitly for the intended constraint.

A written dependency example explains one avoided update anomaly.

assignment.title: Race two clerks without double-allocation
instructions: Use two controlled database sessions and a synchronization barrier to reproduce an overlapping-lease race in a disposable fixture database.
Implement one documented safe protocol, such as locking the unit row before validating the interval, and bound transaction retries.
Post the same fictional receipt twice and inject a failure between receipt insertion and allocation.
deliverables: Failure/rollback transcript with a short design explanation
acceptanceCriteria: Across 20 synchronized races, at most one overlapping lease commits for a unit.
Duplicate receipt requests do not increase allocated payment totals.
The injected mid-transaction failure leaves neither a half-posted receipt nor a changed balance.
Locks and retries have explicit bounds; error cases do not hang indefinitely.

questions.prompt: Why must the overlap check and lease insertion share the same protected transaction?
questions.answer: Otherwise another transaction can change the relevant state between the check and insertion.
questions.explanation: Protection must cover the entire invariant-preserving decision, not just the final write.

reviewPrompts: Which row exists even when a unit has no lease?

assignment.title: Promote a data product without copying production state
instructions: Create separate local dev/test configuration and a CI definition that runs the contract, quality and replay tests before producing a versioned artifact.

questions.prompt: Why can reverting a Git commit fail to undo a destructive data migration?

questions.explanation: Code versioning and data-state recovery are separate mechanisms.

instructions: Use a fixed-seed dataset of at most 100,000 events and compare full reload, incremental load and one layout/partition improvement.
Measure five runs per option, recording elapsed time, bytes/files and available engine statistics while verifying identical logical outputs.
Produce a three-scenario cost worksheet with dated pricing assumptions if actual pricing is used; otherwise label all rates as hypothetical. Include a stop/export plan for any optional Fabric trial.

The recommendation addresses at least one latency/cost trade-off and does not invent savings or a guaranteed speedup.

limitations: This artifact is a curriculum and assessment handoff, not an implementation, completed course record or claim that the learner already has any unmentioned skill. Every module, lesson, assignment, project and milestone is explicitly completed:false.

Common Foundation / Start Here is an application-level prerequisite. No undefined cross-track module IDs are inserted. Canonical concept tags identify shared Python, SQL, testing, Git, Linux-adjacent operation, math/aggregation, security and software-engineering interfaces; tags do not automatically award completion or make a specialist application identical to a foundation lesson.

Estimates include selected lectures/readings, original lab work and review for someone who has completed Common Foundation. Tool installation, troubleshooting, a full reading of every cited textbook chapter and the six complete portfolio projects can require additional time. Prior experience does not auto-complete the work.

Verification was public, read-only HTTP/web_fetch and course/TOC metadata inspection. No shared Playwright browser, sign-in, enrollment, account/profile change or repository modification was used. Author-listed recordings were not played; no HEAD-only response is presented as proof of playability, availability in India or embedding permission.

No PDF, video or book payload was downloaded. The Database Design Digital PDF URL was discovered on the authorized owner page. The implementation must validate the actual file and retain its attribution, license, B.C. Open Collection notice and separately credited material before serving it.

Database Design is the only book flagged redistribution:permitted. Wilke's manuscript and Google's SRE book have explicit CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 notices, but remain link-only because commercial status, modification policy and a suitable official downloadable artifact were not established. Database System Concepts and The Definitive Guide to DAX remain copyrighted link-only books.

Some specified book readings require a legal purchased/library copy. Free author materials and official documentation are supplied for practical learning without a purchase, but they are not misrepresented as the full paid books. Publisher pages for some initially considered O'Reilly titles were inaccessible; those titles were not included.

The referenced books and some videos predate 2026. Their durable concepts are supplemented with current documentation. Do not reuse historical cloud pricing, product-preview status, exact menus, runtime versions, quotas or support claims without checking the chosen environment.

Zoomcamp material uses several non-Microsoft tools. The curriculum selects concepts and permits an equivalent local/Fabric implementation; it does not require mastering GCP, BigQuery, Kestra, dbt, Flink, Kafka and every vendor named in the source. Module 6 should use one compatible streaming stack, not all of them.

Some source notes make overbroad statements about RAG eliminating hallucinations or late events always updating aggregates. This curriculum does not adopt those claims. Learners must test actual engine/output-mode semantics and distinguish retrieval-data quality from AI answer correctness.

Fabric trial access is conditional and time-limited; current checked documentation describes a 60-day trial with feature restrictions. Private Link, Trusted Workspace Access and some AI experiences are not available in that trial. Do not start subscriptions, incur cloud charges, alter a shared tenant or reuse workplace capacity as an implicit part of a lesson.

A local simulation or Spark/Delta equivalent does not prove live Fabric deployment, managed identity, network isolation, cloud capacity consumption or live CDC operation. Label substitutions explicitly and leave the corresponding real-platform evidence gate incomplete until exercised in an authorized environment.

Original assignments use synthetic fixtures and original questions. No copyrighted chapter passages, exam questions, problem solutions, employer assets, credentials or private biometric/customer data are included. The official LeetCode SQL study-plan request returned HTTP 403, so it was not inserted as a falsely verified practice dependency.

Historical A-project completion in the brief is user-reported and does not initialize reconstruction progress. B projects remain planned. Report only actual implementation dates and measured results after the learner produces evidence.

Security/privacy labs are bounded engineering exercises, not regulatory advice or certification. Applicability of Indian or other jurisdictional retention, consent and deletion obligations must be established with appropriate organizational/legal guidance before real use.

The research does not claim the supplied lab designs have already been executed against the user's software versions. The artifact is structurally validated; the implementation/learner must execute labs, assess evidence and maintain resource links over time.
